title: raincloud manifest (sources.json)
description: JSON Schema for sources.json, the manifest that drives the raincloud pipeline. Companion to sources.schema.md (the human-friendly reference). Validated by `python -m raincloud.pipeline.validate_manifest`. Note: `transform.handler` is intentionally not enum-constrained here — the validator cross-checks it against `HANDLERS` in raincloud/_registry.py, the only place a handler is declared, so this schema doesn't need updating every time a handler is added.

schema_version.description: Manifest schema version (1 or 2). Bumping this creates outputs/v{n}/ alongside outputs/v1/. The within-version layout is outputs/v{n}/<slug>/<format>/<filename> (e.g. parquet/<slug>.parquet, vortex/<slug>.vortex, arrow/<slug>.arrow.zstd). v2 adds the canonical Arrow spine and the per-slug `export` block, which is then the only declaration of a dataset's formats in a manifest being authored: `convert` and write.output / write.page_index are v1 only, and this schema rejects them in v2. v2 catalogs released before that rule may still carry `convert.vortex: false`; readers keep treating such a spec (with no export.formats) as Parquet-only. Code accepts both versions; sources.json selects v2.

notes.description: Free-form metadata about the manifest itself. Object or string.

export_priority.description: Catalog-wide writer preference: the default for every dataset without its own export.priority. Same shape as export.priority; a format it does not name falls through to the machine's RAINCLOUD_EXPORT_PRIORITY, then the built-in order. Omit the key for no catalog-wide preference (null is not accepted).

slug.description: kebab-case identifier (a few legacy nyc-tlc slugs use snake_case); matches outputs/v{n}/<slug>/parquet/<slug>.parquet.

kind.description: Reference type. `dataset_card` rarely needs a separate entry since `license.source_url` typically points there; reserve `references` for canonical paper / blog / homepage / source-repo links.

references.description: Optional canonical references for the dataset beyond `license.source_url`. Most useful for surfacing the underlying paper or the project homepage in the TUI.

tags.description: Closed-vocab data-kind tags (0–3) describing the *content shape* a slug exercises (URLs / prose / enums / identifiers / code / timestamps / embeddings / counts / money / measurements / coordinates / binary blobs / nested JSON). Used by the TUI faceted side panel and `list_datasets --tag`. See `raincloud/pipeline/discovery.py:TAG_VOCAB` for the authoritative list.

advisory.description: Required on a derived dataset: why a reader probably wants the parent instead -- takedown rates, copyright posture, expected null prevalence. Shown by `raincloud describe`, which the warning every load emits points to.

spdx.description: SPDX id, or free-form token if no SPDX assignment exists. Describes the aggregator's declared license — see `scrape_advisory` for the gap between that and any uncleared underlying content.

scrape_advisory.description: Heavy asterisk for datasets that aggregate or reference content whose underlying licenses have not been individually cleared (public-web scrapes, Common Crawl derivatives, image/code corpora distributed under takedown models). When non-null, the text renders as a prominent warning in datasets.md, list_datasets --long, and the TUI. `spdx` still describes the aggregator's declared license; this field captures the gap between that and the unclaimed status of the underlying content.

type.description: Where the bytes come from. For `custom`, `notes` names the fetcher: a CUSTOM_FETCHERS entry in raincloud/_registry.py (the slug when notes is null).

urls.description: List of upstream URLs to fetch in order. May be empty when fetch.type="custom" (the custom fetcher resolves its URLs at run time, e.g. Public BI workloads) or "generated".

requires_interactive_accept.description: Marks datasets gated behind a one-time terms-of-use click-through on the upstream's web UI. Valid on fetch.type=kaggle (Kaggle dataset ToS) and fetch.type=huggingface (HF gated repos like LAION). Both fetchers catch the 401/403 and surface a 'visit URL, click Accept, re-run' message regardless of this flag — setting it lets the orchestrator announce the requirement up front.

hf_allow_patterns.description: huggingface-only: glob patterns passed through to snapshot_download(allow_patterns=...). Lets a slug fetch a subset of a giant repo (e.g. just one config or sample of fineweb) without paying for the whole corpus. Null/omitted = whole repo.

hf_revision.description: huggingface-only: git revision (branch, tag, or commit SHA) passed through to snapshot_download(revision=...). Null/omitted = whatever main resolves to at fetch time.

notes.description: Free-form note. For fetch.type="custom" it is load-bearing: it names the CUSTOM_FETCHERS entry in raincloud/_registry.py that fetches this dataset (the slug is used when it is null).

type.description: How fetched files are unpacked. `tar` handles .tar, .tar.gz and .tgz.

options.description: Reader-specific kwargs. Shape varies by reader — see raincloud/pipeline/parse.py.

handler.description: Name of a handler declared in `HANDLERS` in raincloud/_registry.py (raincloud/pipeline/handlers/__init__.py only resolves those names). Validated by validate_manifest.py.

output.description: schema_version 1 only (rejected in v2): the output filename, which no writer read; files are always <format>/<slug>.<ext>.

row_group_size_rows.description: Backstop cap on rows in one row group, in every Parquet writer. Groups are sized by ENCODED bytes (128 MiB by default, RAINCLOUD_ROW_GROUP_TARGET_ENCODED_BYTES; parquet@java counts closed pages at their compressed size, so its groups come out larger); this only catches shapes bytes cannot, such as a single narrow integer column that would otherwise reach ~134M rows per group. NOT a target: set it too low and it binds before the byte target, which is exactly what the former 1048576 did. The manifest convention is 10000000.

page_index.description: schema_version 1 only (rejected in v2): never read by any writer.

Write.description: Parquet writer settings. parquet@py honours all three of compression, row_group_size_rows and statistics. The sidecar writers (parquet@rs, parquet@java, parquet@hardwood) receive row_group_size_rows as RAINCLOUD_ROW_GROUP_MAX_ROWS in their environment, so the recipe's row cap wins in every lane; they choose their own compression and statistics.

row_stability.description:
How the upstream row count evolves over time:
  static     — frozen snapshot (Kaggle dump, archived release, Wikipedia 2024 dump). expect.rows is contractual; drift is a bug.
  grow_only  — append-only live source (NYC OpenData, NOAA observations); past rows don't change.
  mutable    — past records may be revised or deleted (some live CKAN portals).
  null/absent — unclassified.

vortex.description: v1: true emits a sibling <slug>.vortex beside the parquet.

vortex_skip_reason.description: v1: why the Vortex sibling is opted out. Required (non-null string) when vortex=false; must be null when vortex=true. Shown by `list_datasets --no-vortex --json` and the TUI detail pane.

Convert.description: schema_version 1 only: the pre-spine Vortex opt-in. v2 declares formats in `export.formats`.

Hydrate.description: Which of the parent's URL columns to fetch, and into what. Each fetched column `<into>` is followed by a `_<into>_provenance` struct recording every fetch's outcome.

columns.description: Parent column holding URLs -> the column to add.

blocked_hosts_extra.description: Hostnames to add to the fetch blocklist for this dataset, on top of run-time --block files and (if enabled) URLhaus. Hostnames only -- no schemes, no paths.

Export.description: Per-slug export policy (v2): which formats to materialise from the canonical Arrow spine beyond the always-produced `arrow/<slug>.arrow.zstd`, and which writer makes them. Each format is one file, `<format>/<slug>.<ext>`, whichever writer made it; the catalog records the writer beside the file's sha256. In a v2 manifest this is the only declaration of a dataset's formats; omitted, it exports parquet and vortex.

formats.description: Formats the dataset wants. Replaces the default ["parquet", "vortex"]; [] produces only canonical Arrow. Never `arrow` (the canonical every exporter reads) and never a writer-qualified name — the writer comes from `priority`. A format the planned writer cannot produce for this dataset is not declared here: the build measures the failure and records it, and the catalog shows the format as unavailable with that measurement.

priority.description: This dataset's writer preference. The first writer that exists for a format AND is installed writes it, so a machine without a preferred sidecar falls through. Overrides the catalog's `export_priority`, the machine's RAINCLOUD_EXPORT_PRIORITY and the built-in py-first order, for the formats it covers.

notes.description: Free-form annotation, e.g. why a deliberate policy leaves a format out. Never a writer's technical limitation: that is measured by the build and recorded in the catalog. Shown by `list_datasets --no-vortex` and the TUI for a spec whose formats leave out vortex.

Derive.description: A dataset built from another catalog dataset instead of an upstream source. Today the only derivation is hydration: `<parent>-hydrated`, the parent's rows with some URL columns fetched into bytes. Never built unless named (`raincloud build <parent>-hydrated`).

from.description: Slug of the parent dataset, read from its canonical Arrow.

V2Only.description: What schema_version 2 drops. `export.formats` is the one declaration of which formats a dataset exports, so v1's `convert` block is rejected in a v2 manifest being authored (released v2 catalogs that still carry `convert.vortex: false` keep reading as Parquet-only); `write.output` and `write.page_index` were never read by any writer.

WriterPriority.description: Writer preference, most preferred first. Either a list of writer names, which serves every format and does not fall through, so it must name a writer for each format the dataset exports (a list like ["hardwood"], a Parquet-only writer, leaves Vortex with no writer and its export fails), or a map from format to such a list (e.g. {"parquet": ["rs", "py"]}), which serves only the formats it names; any other format falls through to the next level. validate_manifest rejects a name that is no export writer (`canonical` writes only the Arrow spine).
